title: The Nature of Christian Worship

author.name: Alexander Schmemann
author.bio: Renowned 20th-century Orthodox theologian and Dean of St. Vladimir's Seminary.

shortDescription: A profound contemplation on liturgical assembly, eschatological reality, and the transformative purpose of Christian liturgy.
publicationInfo: Originally published in St. Vladimir's Theological Quarterly, 1965.

title: The Life of St. Basil the Great

author.name: St. Gregory of Nyssa
author.bio: One of the Cappadocian Fathers and brother of St. Basil.

shortDescription: An intimate encomium and theological biography honoring the monastic wisdom, pastoral heroism, and doctrinal steadfastness of St. Basil.
publicationInfo: Patrologia Graeca, Vol. 46, trans. W. Moore, Oxford.

title: The Early Fathers on Unity

author.name: Georges Florovsky
author.bio: Pioneering theologian of the Neopatristic synthesis.

shortDescription: An examination of the apostolic ecclesiology of St. Ignatius of Antioch and St. Irenaeus of Lyons amidst early schisms.
publicationInfo: Collected Works of Georges Florovsky, Vol. 3, Nordland Publishing.

title: Scripture and the Living Tradition

author.name: John Meyendorff
author.bio: Patristic scholar and historian of Byzantine Christianity.

shortDescription: How the Church Fathers read the Scriptures: not as an isolated dead text, but within the Eucharistic life of the Holy Spirit.
publicationInfo: Living Tradition: Orthodox Witness in the Contemporary World, SVS Press.

title: Hesychasm and the Inner Kingdom

author.name: Metropolitan Kallistos Ware
author.bio: Oxford theologian and leading voice on the Philokalia and Christian asceticism.

shortDescription: The practice of silence, watchfulness (nepsis), and the Jesus Prayer as an inward pathway to divine communion.
publicationInfo: Delivered as the Fr. Georges Florovsky Lecture, Princeton, 1996.

title: Creatio Ex Nihilo and Cosmic Order

author.name: Jaroslav Pelikan
author.bio: Sterling Professor of History at Yale University and master of Christian tradition.

shortDescription: A critical historical investigation into how 2nd-century apologetic theology established the absolute ontological freedom of God.
publicationInfo: The Christian Tradition: A History of the Development of Doctrine, Vol. 1, Univ. of Chicago Press.
